title: EXP-046 — Hello World Part 2: Two FX_UMs Test Records and Runtime Persistence
objective: Through the existing FX_UMs Web Client runtime Form, establish an unfiltered zero-record baseline for the primary collection, then insert exactly two records into the existing factory-owned FX_UMs SQL table in the dbo schema: FX_UM = EA with FX_Description = Each, and FX_UM = DZ with FX_Description = Dozen. Verify both rows before using exactly one ordinary toolbar Save. Close and reopen the runtime Form through supported native navigation, perform one fresh collection query, and verify that exactly those two records and their values are recovered. Stop before mutation if collection emptiness, field mapping, Form identity, or safe entry behavior cannot be established. The experiment tests same-session runtime persistence only.

in_scope: Inspect the existing FX_UMs Web Client runtime Form and its two bound fields.
Use the existing FX_UMs IDO and factory-owned FX_UMs SQL table without altering their definitions.
Verify the target runtime Form identity and existing authenticated session before any mutation.

Use the accepted EXP-042-R3 empty-criteria collection query and status-bar emptiness gate before entry. Count rule (operator decision 2026-10-10, accepted in EXP-042-R3): in add mode the status bar counts the uncommitted new-row placeholder as an object. Emptiness is established when, immediately after one empty-criteria query (Filter-in-Place F4 with empty criteria, or Refresh), ALL of the following hold: the grid shows exactly one row; that row carries the blue new-row star; both inputs are blank; and the status bar reads exactly (Object 1 of 1). Any unstarred row, any other count, or non-blank inputs closes the gate. After the Save and after the reopen query, the status bar should count exactly the two persisted records (plus the placeholder only if add mode is active; record the exact text and which applies). If the status bar is absent, record that and stop.

Field mapping: the runtime captions read Unit of Measure (FX_UM, Required) and Description (FX_Description), per EXP-045 T14/T15 evidence and the Designer bindings FX_UMEdit = object.FX_UM, FX_DescriptionEdit = object.FX_Description. Edit > Find Value in Collection is used only if the rendered captions differ from this.
Use Edit > Find Value in Collection read-only if field mapping is ambiguous.
Insert only EA / Each and DZ / Dozen, one record at a time.
Perform exactly one ordinary runtime toolbar Save after both records are entered and visually verified.
Close and reopen FX_UMs once through supported Web Client controls, then perform one fresh collection query.
Capture screenshots and concise observations under evidence/EXP-046/.
Create or modify only the EXP-046 experiment record and evidence files in the repository.
out_of_scope: Creating or changing Form, IDO, property-class, string-resource, project, or SQL-table definitions.
Modifying any table other than the existing factory-owned FX_UMs table.
Creating additional records or changing preexisting application records.
Designer editing, metadata synchronization, configuration changes, or deployment.
Check-in, check-out, source-control changes, or metadata unloading.
Direct SQL, internal APIs, browser JavaScript, or unsupported data-writing mechanisms.
Testing business logic, validation rules beyond the two authorized records, or concurrency.
Claims of database-level durability, cross-session persistence, or replay verification.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not enter any record until the exact FX_UMs runtime Form and a reliable zero-record primary-collection baseline are demonstrated.
Do not treat (Object 1 of 1) as emptiness unless every condition of the accepted EXP-042-R3 count rule in scope holds; never treat a filtered or unqueried view as emptiness.
Do not use a filtered zero-match result as proof that the entire collection is empty.
Do not insert either record if EA, DZ, or any other existing collection record is found during the emptiness gate.
Do not edit, delete, overwrite, or repair preexisting records.
Do not change fields other than FX_UM and FX_Description.
Do not perform more than two record insertions or more than one explicit toolbar Save.
Do not repeat an ambiguous Save or record-insertion action.
Do not proceed after an unexpected implicit commit, validation error, Save or discard prompt, timeout, authentication prompt, or other unexplained state.
Do not attempt session recovery, refresh, alternate APIs, or broader navigation to bypass a failed prerequisite.
Do not perform metadata changes, browser-code execution, or repository modifications outside EXP-046.
Limit browser recovery to one fresh snapshot and one corrected inspection, then stop and record the blocker.
Do not promote the procedure to replay_verified from this single execution.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight: screenshot shows the authenticated Web Client, exact FX_UMs runtime Form, expected Unit of Measure and Description fields, and no unexpected prompt. Record that the existing FX_UMs User-scope definition was established in EXP-045. No mutation has occurred.

Field mapping: visible evidence confirms Unit of Measure maps to FX_UM and Description maps to FX_Description, using prior accepted component-binding evidence or the supported Find Value in Collection route if necessary. No unrelated field is selected for entry.

Empty-collection gate: an empty-criteria query with no retained restrictive filter produces a settled, reliable zero-record result for the entire primary collection. Capture the query state and status-bar or other supported zero-record indicator together. If emptiness is ambiguous, the entry gate fails.
First record: before the toolbar Save, the runtime collection visibly contains a newly entered record with FX_UM exactly EA and FX_Description exactly Each. Capture the row and both values.

Second record: before the toolbar Save, the runtime collection visibly contains both authorized rows, EA / Each and DZ / Dozen, with distinct keys and matching descriptions. No third record or modified unrelated field is observed.

Save: exactly one ordinary toolbar Save is invoked after both values are verified. Capture the immediate result, any product message and resulting Save state. An ambiguous result is not retried or counted as successful persistence.

Runtime lifecycle: after the successful Save, FX_UMs closes normally without an unexpected Save or discard prompt and reopens exactly once through supported native Web Client navigation. Capture the closed state and reopened Form identity.

Recovery: one fresh empty-criteria collection query after reopen visibly retrieves exactly two records: EA / Each and DZ / Dozen. Capture both keys and descriptions, the collection-count evidence, and the absence of an unsaved-change indication. If the UI cannot establish cardinality reliably, qualify the finding rather than claiming exactly two stored rows.

Final evidence audit: reconcile entry, Save, close, reopen, query and recovery counts; document the initial zero-record gate and final result; inventory the two authorized data rows and all preexisting objects left untouched; record screenshots and repository confinement. Classify the result as observed only, with database-durability and cross-session limitations.

initial_instruction: T1 — READ-ONLY PREFLIGHT ONLY for EXP-046. Review EXP-042-R3's accepted runtime data-entry method and EXP-045's final runtime evidence. Inspect the inherited Web Client using a fresh snapshot. Confirm authenticated state, the exact existing FX_UMs Form, its two visible field captions and bindings, and the availability of the supported collection-query and status-count controls. Inspect whether any filter or pending unsaved state is present. Establish the reliable unfiltered zero-record gate through the accepted empty-criteria query method, capturing the query criteria, settled result and authoritative zero-record indicator. If field mapping is uncertain, inspect the supported Edit > Find Value in Collection route without making changes. Capture evidence of target identity, field mapping and collection emptiness under evidence/EXP-046/. Do not enter EA or DZ, open an insertion action, invoke Save, close the Form, or change any resource during T1. If the zero-record result cannot be proven, stop and report the blocker. Leave the runtime Form available for a separately reviewed entry task. Report exact visible observations, counts, screenshot paths and limitations.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261010-214137-Ia7F. Rationale: EXP-044 established the existing FX_UMs table and IDO, and EXP-045 established the User-scope Multi-View Form, its field bindings, captions, Save, and runtime rendering. The next controlled capability is inserting application data through that Form. Reuse the accepted EXP-042-R3 runtime entry method, but treat this as a new observation on a different IDO and table, not a clean replay. The existing FX_UMs runtime tab from EXP-045 is the preferred starting point. | Operator review: the 'Object 1 of 1' prohibition replaced by the accepted EXP-042-R3 count rule (the draft would have made the emptiness gate impossible); field mapping from EXP-045 bindings and captions; exact-value guard FX_UMs/Each/Dozen (EA and DZ are not listed because the case-insensitive guard would then block typing 'Each' and 'Dozen'; they are checked through AC-4/AC-5 evidence instead); no-JavaScript policy. Data values EA/DZ are tutorial values inside the factory-owned table dbo.FX_UMs (later FX_Items rows reference them). Approved by the operator 2026-10-10 with precondition attestation: logged in, configuration OK, Web Client loaded, no unsaved changes.
